title: Ultra-small-angle graphene twistronics with monolayer spacers: From interlayer hybridisation and moiré effects to high-temperature magnetotransport oscillations
authors: Benjamin Fuller, Haowei Fan, Agustin Montemurro, Yuyuan Pan, Alexey I. Berdyugin, Vladimir I. Falko, Xiao Li
abstract: Based on the analysis of moiré superlattice characteristics and interlayer hybridisation in small-angle twisted graphene multilayers with a monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) spacer, we predict spectral features and quantum transport effects in these systems. Here, we consider both a twisted bilayer and double bilayers with a spacer, discuss double bilayers in two stacking orders - with and without inversion symmetry - and also compare the results obtained with self-consistent Hartree calculations with and without in-plane periodic charge distribution, offering computationally efficient models for these graphene/hBN/graphene moiré systems. We note parametric intervals where the appearance of minibands can be enhanced by tuning with an out-of-plane displacement field, and identify the miniband edges and van Hove singularities across a broad range of densities and displacement fields. These system host Lifshitz transitions at which the Fermi lines form a network across moiré Brillouin zones, and to which Brown-Zak oscillations converge at low magnetic field and elevated temperatures. We analyse interlayer hybridisation across the same parameter space, discuss how hybridisation affects in-plane magneto-transport in ultra-high-mobility structures, and predict that semiclassical magneto-oscillations of interlayer hybridisation can lead to 1/B-periodic quantum oscillations of resistivity persistent to high temperature.
summary: This work theoretically models quantum transport in twisted graphene multilayers separated by hBN spacers. By analyzing moiré superlattice effects and interlayer hybridization, the authors predict the formation of minibands and the emergence of persistent $1/B$-periodic quantum oscillations in resistivity. This provides a detailed framework for understanding tunable quantum electronic properties in van der Waals heterostructures.
main_problem: The study investigates the spectral features and quantum transport effects in small-angle twisted graphene multilayers separated by a hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) spacer.
main_result: The system exhibits minibands, hosts Lifshitz transitions, and predicts $1/B$-periodic quantum oscillations in resistivity due to semiclassical magneto-oscillations of interlayer hybridization.
method: The analysis employs a hybrid k.p-theory–tight-binding (HkpTB) approach, utilizing self-consistent Hartree mean-field calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system is MLG/hBN/MLG or BLG/hBN/BLG, modeled using Hamiltonians that account for moiré interlayer tunneling, which is significantly weaker than direct contact.
key_observables: Density of States (DoS), miniband edges, van Hove singularities, interlayer hybridization ($\Pi$), and magnetotransport oscillations (Brown-Zak oscillations, $1/B$-periodic oscillations).
important_parameters: Twist angles ($	heta = 0.2^\circ, 0.5^\circ$), out-of-plane displacement field, and magnetic field ($B$).
main_assumptions: The spacer is assumed to be a monolayer hBN, and the analysis often compares results with and without in-plane periodic charge distribution.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate microscopic structures and exemplary dispersions for the different graphene/hBN/graphene systems, and show DoS maps and magnetotransport results.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the Hamiltonian for different bilayer configurations (MLG/hBN/MLG, BLG/hBN/BLG) to performing self-consistent calculations, analyzing key transport diagnostics like hybridization and magnetotransport, and finally discussing the physical implications of these findings.
why_interesting: The detailed modeling of moiré superlattices and the prediction of high-temperature quantum oscillations in weakly coupled 2D materials are highly relevant to understanding emergent quantum phenomena in engineered quantum systems.
